title: Too much play time without meaningful progress
evidence: 72% of all play time of `best_roi` is spent in stretches longer than 5 min before purchases add up to +5% income (33 dead zones, 451 min in total). 27 of them fit inside a single session (*idle sessions*): the offline earnings are spent in the first seconds of a 10-minute session and the rest of the session adds almost nothing.
action: Give the session itself something to do: raise active income relative to offline (lower `offline.efficiency` 0.5 → 0.35, or raise `tap.upgrades.showman.value`), and/or add short in-session goals in the game design (NPC events while playing, timed boosts). In the economy, more mid-sized purchases per tier (a 4th staff type, more equipment levels) also break up the waits.

title: Long wait for `coo`
evidence: On day 6.2 (stage: restaurant (run 1)) the player waits **70 min of play** (≈ 7 sessions, 2.2 d calendar) until `coo`; meanwhile only 0 small purchases.
action: The manager `coo` is too expensive right after its tier opens (the tier earns nothing offline until then). Lower `tiers.franchise.managers.coo.cost`: 10T → **1.4T**.

title: Long wait for `franchise`
evidence: On day 4.0 (stage: restaurant (run 1)) the player waits **70 min of play** (≈ 7 sessions, 2.2 d calendar) until `franchise`; meanwhile only 2 small purchases (mostly `head_chef`).
action: Wall before **franchise**. Keep the pacing target and fill the gap with content in the `restaurant` tier: e.g. a 4th staff item with `base_cost` ≈ 5.3B and `income` ≈ 280K (base payback ~1.6x the last staff), or more levels on `interior` (`max_level` +5). Lowering `tiers.franchise.unlock_cost` also helps but moves the franchise milestone earlier.

title: The restaurant stage carries 61% of the journey
evidence: In run 1 the player spends 5.8 d (165 min of play) in restaurant with 3 staff, 2 upgrades and 1 manager(s) to buy.
action: Either add content to `restaurant` (another staff type and 1-2 upgrades), or move the stage boundary: lower the next tier's cost and raise the target accordingly.

title: first_prestige is too fast
evidence: `first_prestige` (first prestige in about two weeks): reached after 4.8 h of play / 9.4 d calendar; target 7.0 h of play (= 14.0 d calendar). Status: **too fast** (x0.69).
action: Lever has no measurable effect; adjust the previous stage instead.

title: Offline earnings dominate
evidence: From day 2 on, 93% of `best_roi`'s coins come from offline earnings; the 10-minute sessions add little beyond spending.
action: Fine for a relaxed idle game. If sessions should matter more, lower `offline.efficiency` (0.5 → 0.35) or reduce manager `offline_cap_hours_add`, and re-run `tune` (pacing will slow down).

title: `cheapest` stalls before cafe
evidence: `cheapest` reaches `cafe` after 5.0 h vs 8.5 min for `best_roi` (same sessions, different buying).
action: Players who buy naively get stuck: show a 'best buy' hint in the UI, and/or steepen `cost_growth` of the cheapest generators (e.g. `nephew` 1.12 → 1.14) so cheap items stop soaking up cash.

title: Saving for cafe beats greedy ROI
evidence: `saver` reaches `cafe` after 5.8 min vs 8.5 min for `best_roi`.
action: The cafe unlock is worth more than its immediate income gain suggests (its global multiplier and new items). Fine as a skill expression; if unwanted, lower `tiers.cafe.global_income_mult`.

title: Tap share is healthy
evidence: After day 1 taps make 27% of the income earned while playing (1.8% of all income incl. offline).

title: Prestige loop works
evidence: Run 2 reaches franchise x1.6 faster than run 1 (x2.12 income from 56 reputation).

title: `casual` pace is acceptable
evidence: `casual` reaches `franchise` after 12.0 d vs 6.2 d (x1.9, warning above x3).
